name: QuickBooks Online
tagline: Small-business accounting, invoicing, expenses, payroll add-ons, and tax workflows

priorArt.desc: Open-source accounting software for invoicing, expenses, and small-business books.

notes: Essential no/kinda: the UI is cloneable, financial trust is not.
prompt:
Honest answer: don't. QuickBooks is accounting correctness, bank feeds, payroll, and the
fact that your accountant already lives in it. A one-shot clone of the books your taxes
depend on is a liability, not a saving.

If you genuinely just invoice a few clients and track expenses, here is the safe
personal slice:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, binds to localhost, no hosting.
- Invoices: client, line items, tax rate, due date; render to PDF with Playwright's
  page.pdf; mark paid by hand.
- Expenses: import your bank's CSV export, categorize with a rule table that auto-
  matches repeat payees, edit the rest by hand.
- Reports: a cash-basis P&L and per-quarter totals, plus CSV export of everything for
  the accountant.
- No accounts, no telemetry, the books never leave your machine; back up the SQLite
  file.
- Out of scope: bank feeds, reconciliation, payroll, and anything that files taxes. When
  the numbers start to matter, pay for real software or an accountant.
- README: state plainly that this is bookkeeping-lite, not accounting.
